Well, I can certainly relate to the idea of wanting to set boundaries for a new technology user, whether it's a baby with a smartphone or an adult with a computer! In psychology, we often talk about something called "cyberparenting," which involves setting guidelines and using parental controls to help children navigate the digital world safely.

Here are a few tips for setting up parental controls on a smartphone:

1. Set up screen time limits: Many devices have built-in tools for setting daily or weekly limits on screen time. You can also set specific times of day when the device is off-limits.
2. Block inappropriate content: Most devices allow you to block certain apps or websites that you don't want your child to access.
